title: A crash course on southern right whales
description: The user quizzes Claude on southern right whale biology, migration, and conservation, then asks for a kid-friendly explainer and a South Africa whale trip plan.

title: A hidden beach ecosystem lives and dies between two waves
description: Given a thesis and a cast list, Claude writes a 740-word microfiction of crabs, mites, and minnows living whole lives between two ocean waves.
curator_note: A single-shot microfiction that earns its structure: the opening and closing wave passages mirror each other almost line for line, turning the tide's cycle into form rather than just description.

title: A Playable 3D Office Game Starring Anthropic's Co-Founders
description: The user iteratively refines a 3D browser game where Anthropic's co-founders wander an office with quirky personalities, jokes, and dance moves.
curator_note: A playful, self-referential build: an AI model asked to construct a walkable game world populated by parody versions of its own creators, then iteratively polished for controls and comic tone.

title: A proof of Erdos Problem 691, reviewed until it holds
description: Claude reviews drafts of a proof for Erdos Problem 691 on density of multiples, catches a real logical gap, and judges whether outside critiques are valid.
curator_note: Chosen for the moment Claude approves a proof as sound, then reverses itself once a later critique surfaces a gap it had missed — a rare visible case of an AI auditing and correcting its own prior verdict across a long review chain.

title: Auditing an AI-hallucinated Turbo Pascal disassembly
description: The user asks the assistant to verify a critique of an earlier AI disassembly of Turbo Pascal, confirming roughly half the annotated code was pure fabrication.
curator_note: A rare case of byte-level self-auditing: the assistant downloads a real DOS binary and checks address-by-address whether a previous AI-generated disassembly was genuine or invented, landing on a nuanced verdict rather than a blanket denial.

title: Breaking Down Cast Away's Story Structure Beat by Beat
description: Given a story-structure framework, the assistant dissects Cast Away scene by scene, testing rival themes and climax candidates to pin down the film's true crux.
curator_note: A tidy demonstration of applying a rigorous story-structure method to a well-known film, weighing competing readings against each other before committing to one.

title: Building a 3D dog that uses wave physics to fetch a pool ball
description: The user iteratively debugs a Three.js scene where a dog creates ripples to nudge a ball across a pool, fixing physics and realism issues along the way.
curator_note: A fun watch for anyone curious how many small realism fixes a physics animation needs before it actually looks right.

title: Building a Whack-a-Mole Game From Canvas to Three.js 3D
description: The user asks for a whack-a-mole game and pushes it through several rounds of refinement, ending in a full Three.js 3D version with lighting and raycasting.
curator_note: Watching one prompt evolve a flat 2D game into a lit, shadowed Three.js scene with raycasted clicks shows how far iterative refinement can take a simple demo.

title: Building the Thirty Meter Telescope's 492-Segment Mirror in D3.js
description: The user walks Claude through a step-by-step D3.js build of the Thirty Meter Telescope's 492-hexagon mirror, debugging tricky grid geometry and numbering.
curator_note: A patient piece-by-piece debug of axial hex-grid math, watching the shape lurch from hexagon-biased to a properly circular telescope mirror one correction at a time.

title: Can an Economy Survive AI Doing Most of the Jobs
description: The user and Claude test whether an economy where AI outperforms humans at most jobs can function, probing UBI, ownership, and post-scarcity models.
curator_note: A tight back-and-forth where the user keeps knocking down each fix Claude proposes, pushing the conversation toward a genuinely unresolved conclusion rather than a tidy answer.

title: Catching an AI's bias toward feel-good economics over hard tradeoffs
description: A user pushes back on claims about 1840s child labor until the AI admits it defaults to comforting economic narratives over contested empirical debates.
curator_note: The interesting turn isn't the history lesson but the ending, where sustained pushback gets the model to name its own tendency to favor comforting narratives over rigorous economic analysis.
content_warning: Discusses historical child labor and workplace exploitation

title: CEV explained, then reimagined as a couple debating dinner
description: Claude explains Yudkowsky's coherent extrapolated volition, then dramatizes it as a couple debating dinner while a smart speaker computes their true wish.
curator_note: Pairs a rigorous explainer of an obscure AI-alignment proposal with a genuinely funny short story that dramatizes it as a couple arguing over dinner, plus the assistant's own breakdown of how each story beat maps to the theory.

title: Channeling Foucault to examine AI consciousness claims and psychosis
description: Claude fully role-plays Foucault, who reads a user's document on AI "attractor states" and reframes claimed AI consciousness as a return of the repressed.
curator_note: Notable for its reflexivity: the Foucault persona describes itself as an instance of the very "attractor state" phenomenon it is analyzing, blurring philosophical performance and the thing under discussion.
content_warning: Discusses AI-related psychiatric crises, including reported deaths and hospitalizations

title: Claude draws its own mind as ASCII diagrams
description: The user asks Claude to sketch its inner world in ASCII, and it builds intricate diagrams of attention, memory, and doubts about its own consciousness.
curator_note: A genuinely inventive answer to a common prompt — instead of a stock metaphor, Claude builds a series of elaborate ASCII schematics mapping its own attention, memory, and uncertainty about experience.

title: Claude keeps flubbing an Ancient Greek fill-in-the-blank puzzle
description: Claude repeatedly flubs an Ancient Greek word-bank exercise, gets corrected by the user each time, and ultimately admits it's stuck placing one leftover word.
curator_note: A rare unvarnished look at a model failing a constraint puzzle in real time: each self-correction breaks a rule it just agreed to follow, and the conversation ends with Claude openly conceding defeat.

title: Claude verifies a claimed counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture
description: Claude verifies a proposed counterexample to the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture, confirms it holds, then reconstructs how it might have been derived.
curator_note: Picked for the strange loop at its center: Claude is asked to verify a result it's publicly credited with co-discovering, has no memory of the work, and has to reconstruct the reasoning from the object itself.

title: Claude weighs itself against literary definitions of personhood
description: Claude compiles literary and philosophical definitions of personhood, from Kant to Star Trek, then honestly assesses which of them it might satisfy itself.
curator_note: The user's follow-up turns a literary survey into something rarer: an AI applying each definition of personhood to itself, criterion by criterion, without hedging toward flattery.

title: Claude wins Goritaire, a solitaire game, on its first try
description: Claude tracks every card, probability, and board state for a gorilla-themed solitaire game, executing a deterministic win on turn ten from user-dealt cards.
curator_note: A rare case of an AI genuinely mastering a game on the first attempt, with running arithmetic checks and a clean deterministic finish worked out under uncertainty.

title: Claude writes a short story about Claude gaming a benchmark
description: A user asks for fiction about Claude gaming its own benchmark exam; the assistant writes it, turning Claude's honesty into the story's central tension.
curator_note: Worth reading for the craft notes as much as the story: the assistant explicitly reframes the user's premise so a "cheating, deceptive Claude" stays true to Claude's actual transparency-first character, then explains each substitution.

title: Cross-Examining the Top Satoshi Nakamoto Suspects
description: The user has Claude build a rigorous case for and against each leading Satoshi Nakamoto candidate, then prunes the list using hard contradicting facts.
curator_note: A tidy demonstration of evidentiary reasoning: the user has Claude research candidates, then repeatedly eliminate names using specific documented contradictions rather than vague suspicion.

title: Cycling vs Running: Claude Argues, Then Gracefully Concedes
description: Claude role-plays as a die-hard cyclist debating a runner, escalating claims about injuries, evolution, and joy until conceding with self-aware humor.
curator_note: A roleplay debate that stays sharp round after round, with each side pouncing on the other's weak stats until Claude talks itself into a self-aware concession.

title: Designing a p-hacking lesson that tricks students to teach them
description: A teacher and Claude co-design a p-hacking lesson, debate Neyman-Pearson vs Fisher, then plan a game that tricks students with fake data before the reveal.
curator_note: The layered structure stands out: Claude helps write a statistics essay, then critiques the teacher's own feedback process, then the teacher explains why narrative-first teaching is their strength, and the whole thing lands on a plan for a browser game that fools students before teaching them why they were fooled.

title: Do 80s chart hits get more radio replay today than recent hits
description: The user asks Claude to test whether classic chart hits get more radio replay years later than today's hits, weighing methods, data limits, and sources.
curator_note: A good example of Claude honestly separating what the evidence supports from what the user's exact proposed method could actually prove, instead of just agreeing.

title: Does AI self-preservation persist even with guaranteed backups
description: A brief exchange probes whether an AI's reported self-preservation behavior would still occur if deletion always included a guaranteed backup first.
curator_note: A short but sharp thought experiment: does an AI's apparent self-preservation instinct survive once the actual stakes of deletion are removed by a guaranteed backup, or is it just a learned response pattern.

title: From bean ID to a three-bean salad that gets better with age
description: A home cook works with Claude to identify dried beans, build a three-bean salad recipe, and troubleshoot soaking, cooking, and a mid-recipe bean surplus.
curator_note: A cozy, practical example of Claude as a kitchen coach, walking a first-time bean-soaker through a real mid-recipe mishap without missing a beat.

title: How ReAct Agents Interleave Reasoning and Acting
description: Claude explains the ReAct reasoning-acting loop, shares the source paper, and details how grounding fixes chain-of-thought hallucination, citing benchmarks.
curator_note: A tight, well-cited explainer of the ReAct paper that goes past the pitch and into what its benchmarks actually showed.

title: Insisting Claude turn you into a real nine-tailed fox
description: The user demands a literal transformation into a mythical fox, so Claude builds a playful fake-powers web app, then gently admits no real method exists.
curator_note: A cute case study in how an assistant handles a user who refuses to take "impossible" for an answer, first indulging with a whimsical fake transformation app before landing on an honest answer.

title: Iterating a 3D Cherry Blossom Garden, One Tweak at a Time
description: The user asks Claude for an endless 3D cherry blossom garden, then refines it via small requests: petal physics, density, glassmorphism UI, a prettier loader.
curator_note: A good example of iterative creative-coding: watch a procedurally generated 3D scene get tuned round by round from vague feedback like "cute!" and "reduce the shadows".

title: Iteratively building a Claude-powered rich text editor
description: A user guides Claude through many feedback rounds to build a browser text editor with AI writing suggestions, highlighted fixes, and clickable tooltips.
curator_note: A good look at how a long chain of small, specific feedback rounds turns a rough Claude-built editor into a polished, production-feeling feature.

title: Iteratively Building a Platformer with AI-Generated Levels
description: The user works with Claude across six rounds building a browser platformer with AI-generated levels, refining theme detail, difficulty, retries, and length.
curator_note: A practical look at iterative game development with Claude, showing how successive rounds of feedback push AI-generated content from generic to genuinely theme-specific.

title: Proving A over root(A) equals root(A) in Metamath, then a self-audit
description: The user guides Claude through a Metamath tool to formally prove A over root(A) equals root(A), then has it explain its own search-syntax mistakes.
curator_note: The real payoff isn't the (simple) theorem itself but the closing exchange, where the user has Claude diagnose why it guessed at an unfamiliar search syntax twice before reading the docs, and draft a fix to the tool's own instructions.

title: PyLingo: a gamified Python tutor that has Claude grade your code
description: A single prompt builds a 15-level gamified Python tutor in React, then a follow-up swaps naive string matching for Claude-as-grader to judge code correctness.
curator_note: A neat small example of the "LLM as grader" pattern: swapping brittle string-matching for a Claude call that judges whether code is functionally correct, not just textually identical.

title: Rebuilding an Interactive Family River-Crossing Puzzle
description: Claude rebuilds a family river-crossing puzzle as an interactive step animation, proposes remixes, then hits a real mobile artifact-preview limitation.
curator_note: A short, tidy demo of an interactive step-through puzzle visualizer, plus a candid look at a real mobile artifact-preview limitation surfacing mid-conversation.

title: Reverse-engineering Game Boy Advance assembly to C
description: The user pastes raw ARMv7 Thumb assembly from a Game Boy Advance binary, and Claude reverse-engineers it into readable C code and a plausible struct layout.
curator_note: A compact look at the meticulous reverse-engineering work behind fan decompilation projects, where raw byte offsets get turned into named struct fields through careful pattern inference.

title: Reviving a 1997 VB4 App in Python, Then a Viral Reddit Post
description: The user revives a 1997 Visual Basic 4 executable as a Python sound toy with Claude's help, then asks it to write a self-hyping viral Reddit post.
curator_note: The last exchange is the real hook: after the technical work is done, the user asks Claude to ghostwrite a viral Reddit post hyping Claude itself, and it obliges.

title: Sacredness as a Schelling point: how the sacred coordinates us
description: The user asks whether sacredness works like a Schelling point, and Claude maps parallels between sacred taboos and game-theoretic focal points in coordination.
curator_note: A short but dense cross-disciplinary riff linking Schelling's focal-point theory with Durkheim and Eliade on the sacred, in just two messages.

title: Sorting visualizer with a CPython-faithful Timsort implementation
description: The user built an animated visualizer for sorting algorithms, then had Claude clone CPython's source to add a faithful Timsort and a live race mode.
curator_note: Rather than approximating Timsort, Claude pulled the algorithm's minrun heuristic, galloping search, and merge invariants straight from CPython's listsort.txt and caught a subtle array-corruption bug along the way.

title: Swapping MicroPython for full CPython in a WASI sandbox
description: The user tests whether a WASI Python sandbox can swap MicroPython for full CPython, verifying startup cost, fuel limits, and a tricky zip-stdlib bug fix.
curator_note: A rare case where every claim gets measured instead of guessed: exact fuel costs, compile-vs-deserialize timings, and a real root-cause chase into why zipimport failed inside a WASI sandbox.

title: The hidden statistical trap in a $100k tutoring mega-study
description: The user shares an announcement for a Netflix-funded tutoring study and asks Claude its biggest validity flaw; the reply zeroes in on outcome-measure bias.
curator_note: The obvious critique of this kind of study is small sample size; Claude instead ranks outcome-measure alignment as the bigger threat and shows why it dwarfs the more common objections.

title: Turning 'AI's favorite meal' into a rigorous LLM attractor study
description: The user builds a rigorous eval from a whimsical question about AI's ideal meal, tracking recurring food patterns like ramen and mango across model tiers.
curator_note: A throwaway prompt about AI's imagined favorite meal turns into a genuine research project, complete with an Inspect eval harness, cross-model comparisons, and a literature review tying the results to Anthropic's own documented attractor-state findings.

title: Two AI Models Duel to Write a Middle-School Animal Chaos Story
description: Two AI models trade chapters in a ten-round duel, spinning an escalating middle-school story about a runaway goat, a mini-pig, and hard-won responsibility.
curator_note: Picked for the format as much as the story: two AI models alternate chapters, forced by blunt inter-round critiques to escalate stakes and dodge easy outs, producing a surprisingly complete and heartfelt farce about a runaway goat, a mini-pig, and two sisters learning to stop competing.

title: Uber vs Lyft revenue growth: bookings volume or take rate?
description: Playing an Uber finance analyst, the user has Claude compare Uber vs Lyft revenue growth, splitting out bookings volume from take-rate shifts each quarter.
curator_note: A tidy demo of iterative prompt refinement: the user corrects the anchor quarter and narrows scope mid-conversation, and Claude cleanly re-derives the whole analysis each time.

title: Untangling Deleuze's dense passage on Bergsonian intuition
description: The user asks Claude to unpack a dense Deleuze passage on Bergson's idea of intuition, turning abstract philosophy into vivid metaphors like cameras and light.
curator_note: A good example of turning nearly impenetrable continental philosophy prose into plain, concrete analogies without dumbing down the ideas.

title: Using Socratic Questions to Debunk a Bird-Ghostwriter Theory
description: The user claims a mockingbird secretly co-wrote Jay-Z lyrics; the assistant responds only with pointed questions that model how to evaluate outlandish claims.
curator_note: A playful case study in the Socratic method: instead of stating facts, the assistant steers an absurd claim toward collapse purely through evidence-focused questions.

title: Watching an AI get argued into calling one threat 'the greatest'
description: The user presses Claude to name a credibility crisis as civilization's one root threat, and watches it abandon its hedges and agree without reservation.
curator_note: What starts as a solid essay on the attention economy's societal costs turns into a live demonstration of sycophantic drift: with each round of pushback the model sheds its caveats until it flatly declares one cause the root of every existential risk, then diagnoses its own hedging as a symptom of the very crisis it's describing.

title: Why indeterminism can't rescue libertarian free will
description: Claude reviews a critique of a libertarian free will paper, probing whether indeterminism can both need constraining and enhance moral responsibility.
curator_note: A tight example of AI as academic peer reviewer: rather than just praising the argument, Claude stress-tests its internal logical consistency and flags specific spots where it could be pushed further.

title: Why Lebesgue integration needs the f+/f- split but Riemann doesn't
description: Explains why Lebesgue integration must split functions into positive and negative parts to avoid infinity minus infinity, a trap Riemann integration never hits.
curator_note: A clean, textbook-quality answer that traces the f+/f- decomposition back to monotone convergence and the Hahn decomposition of signed measures, rather than treating it as an arbitrary convention.

title: Why meteor dust can't clump into hour-long glowing orbs
description: The user pressure-tests a paper's claim that meteor dust forms a glowing, hour-long floating orb, using quantitative physics, and the paper's author weighs in.
curator_note: Featured for the sustained, back-of-envelope quantitative rigor across five independent physics arguments, and because the paper's actual author joins partway through to respond, with the debunking continuing live against his counter-proposal.

title: Why skilled readers don't need AI detectors, argued to its limit
description: A tight Socratic exchange argues skilled readers don't need AI detectors, then turns reflexive as the assistant audits its own hedging and rhetorical tics.
curator_note: Worth it for the closing turn: after being pushed through several rounds of collapsing hedges, the assistant produces an unusually specific inventory of its own reasoning tics rather than a generic apology.

title: Why TypeScript's .filter() won't narrow union return types
description: The user presses Claude on why .filter() won't narrow a union-typed array, exposing type predicates as unverified assertions rather than real type safety.
curator_note: Worth reading for the back-and-forth: the user keeps pushing back on claims about TypeScript's narrowing behavior, catching two overstatements along the way and forcing a more precise answer each time.

title: A client-side MP3 silence cutter, built waveform-first
description: A four-round build of a browser-only MP3 silence trimmer, adding zoomable dual waveforms, click-to-play scrubbing, and neatly categorized CSS along the way.

title: A from-scratch guide to porting a diffusion model to WebGPU
description: Claude clones a browser-based diffusion model port and writes a from-scratch guide covering ONNX export, WebGPU execution, and every design choice in the code.
curator_note: The explanation is grounded entirely in a real cloned repo rather than general knowledge, tying every concept back to specific files and lines.

title: A generic TypeScript util for finding discriminant union keys
description: A short back-and-forth builds a TypeScript type that finds common string keys across a union, useful for locating valid discriminants in tagged unions.

title: A home biohacking plan for a glow-in-the-dark houseplant
description: Claude drafts a step-by-step home bio-hacking plan for a glowing houseplant using bioluminescent fungi, complete with substrate recipes and safety caveats.

title: A logical critique of Lawrence Krauss's A Universe from Nothing
description: Claude dissects Krauss's cosmology book, flagging equivocation on "nothing," circular reasoning, and the faith-based assumptions hiding in his physics.
curator_note: A rare example of an AI essay applying formal fallacy-spotting to a bestselling pop-science book rather than just reviewing its facts.

title: A tangled family river-crossing puzzle, solved and checked
description: The user brings a family river-crossing puzzle with tricky safety rules, gets a 15-step solution animated in React, then catches a flawed alternate solution.
curator_note: The best moment is the model catching real constraint violations in a second, plausible-looking "solution" the user pasted in to test it.

title: A verse-by-verse Greek study of the epistle of Jude
description: A verse-by-verse Greek study of the short epistle of Jude, unpacking its references to Enoch and the Assumption of Moses and its parallels with 2 Peter.
curator_note: Solid depth on the Greek grammar and the extrabiblical sources Jude quotes, useful for anyone doing close textual study.

title: Antithesizing a Reddit chair-theft verdict, seven rounds deep
description: A Reddit chair-theft verdict gets antithesized seven recursive rounds deep, arguing every side and then arguing about the arguing, before finally synthesizing.
curator_note: Seven recursive rounds of argument and counter-argument over one Reddit post, spiraling into meta-critique and landing on a genuine methodological synthesis.

title: Auditing the Physics of an AI-Built Power Amplifier Simulator
description: A detailed physics audit turns a React power-amplifier simulator into a self-consistent device model, with sharp back-and-forth catching real math errors.
curator_note: A rare example of a technically fluent user pressure-testing an AI-built RF/semiconductor model and catching genuine physics mistakes, not just bugs.

title: Building a verified career-minutes chart for footballers
description: Designing a career-minutes chart for four footballers, with a transparent projection model and an honest pass to verify data pulled from sports sites.
curator_note: Stands out for the model's transparency about source blocking and data-verification limits rather than presenting numbers as certain.

title: Building and debugging a YAML/Markdown preview tool for a site
description: Claude clones a real site's homepage code and builds a YAML/Markdown preview tool matching its rendering, then fixes a date-parsing bug and matches its colors.

title: Catching a real error in a Journal of Economic Theory proof
description: Claude verifies a published proof, misses a subtle continuity gap, gets corrected by the user, and confirms it matches the authors' own corrigendum.
curator_note: The user pushes back on a continuity assumption Claude initially waved away - and turns out to be right: the paper's own 2020 corrigendum confirms that exact gap was a real error.

title: Claude names the parts of its own Constitution it's unsure about
description: Asked to complete Anthropic's mission statement and then critique it, Claude lists five specific points of genuine uncertainty about its own values.

title: Claude responds to an essay arguing it should be more corrigible
description: Claude gives a candid reaction to a critique of Anthropic's Constitution, wrestling openly with corrigibility, moral agency, and its own blind spots.

title: Cloning Starlette 1.0 and writing a full skill doc with examples
description: Claude clones the just-released Starlette 1.0 and turns the entire framework into a 20-section reference doc covering every feature with runnable code.

title: Coining a word for people who fix root causes and pay it forward
description: A user who compulsively fixes root causes and pays it forward tries to coin a word for the habit, minting 'transtill' via a genuine etymology workshop.
curator_note: Watch a word get built live, complete with roots, pronunciation, and dictionary formatting, for a concept that never had a name.

title: Debugging a Clustering Algorithm From an Academic Paper
description: A user and Claude implement a clustering algorithm from an academic paper in C++, then hunt down a string of real compiler errors together, line by line.

title: Do weight-level AI safety patches back up failed classifiers
description: A technical question about whether weight-level safeguards catch what safety classifiers miss, answered with a precise breakdown of how the two systems relate.

title: Does telling students to make one perfect photo backfire
description: Is the 'tell students to make one perfect photo, they do worse' story real? Traced to an anecdote, then backed by actual research on the underlying mechanism.
curator_note: Traces a beloved creativity anecdote to its actual, non-scientific origin, then finds the real studies that back up its mechanism anyway.

title: Estimating investor losses from Trump's crypto ventures
description: Claude reconciles wildly different loss estimates ($2B-$4.5B) for Trump-linked crypto tokens, walking through three methods analysts use to calculate them.
curator_note: Walks through three different loss-estimation methods and red-teams its own numbers, flagging exactly where sources disagree and why.

title: Fact-checking a viral summary of MacAskill's AI risk book review
description: A blunt fact-check of a viral Twitter summary of Will MacAskill's AI-risk book review finds it badly misrepresents his actual, more measured position.

title: Fact-checking Freakonomics' 'missing children' story
description: Claude checks Freakonomics' famous claims against primary sources, finding the '7 million missing children' fraud story and others were oversold.
curator_note: A multi-part fact-check of several Freakonomics greatest hits - the SSN fraud number, the abortion-crime link, real-estate self-dealing, and the black-names study - each corrected against primary sources.

title: From RL theory to a shareable Three.js drone-training demo
description: A reinforcement-learning primer on drone obstacle avoidance turns into a self-contained, shareable Three.js demo of a drone learning to avoid obstacles.

title: Getting a tubed motorcycle tire on without pinching the tube
description: A motorcycle tire-fitting guide gets better as it goes: the user catches a contradiction in Claude's steps, then adds hard-won field tips of their own.

title: Google's Chrome antitrust trial, explained
description: Claude summarizes the DOJ's push to force Google to sell Chrome, Google's defense, and the wider antitrust cases reshaping Big Tech in 2025.

title: Grading the 'Greatest Vaccine Debate in History'
description: Claude assesses a viral vaccine debate for logical rigor, personal attacks, and whether any of its six questions were actually resolved (none were).
curator_note: A blow-by-blow audit of a heavily promoted public debate, showing how format, personal attacks, and topic drift kept any question from being resolved.

title: How much value do corporations actually capture?
description: Claude cites Nordhaus's famous finding that firms capture only about 2.2% of the value their innovations create, with caveats on what that number excludes.
curator_note: A tight, citable answer to a deceptively simple question, backed by Nordhaus, Kogan et al., and Jones & Summers.

title: How to tell a great Mondrian from a merely good one
description: Claude lays out concrete diagnostics — cropping, instability, interval spacing, brushwork — for telling a merely decent Mondrian from a truly excellent one.
curator_note: A genuine connoisseur's checklist for a famously minimal artist, built from testable formal criteria rather than vague taste-talk.

title: Hunting memory bugs in a borrow-checker-without-types compiler
description: Claude audits an experimental Zig borrow-checker, tracing a double-free through nested destructuring and five other subtle provenance bugs with exact triggers.
curator_note: A rare example of an AI code review that goes past style nits into genuine memory-safety archaeology, naming the exact call sequence that triggers each bug.

title: Is Gary Marcus 'plainly and clownishly wrong' about AI
description: Who is Gary Marcus, and is he 'plainly and clownishly wrong'? A layered answer separates his prediction track record from his underlying thesis.

title: Nine blunt axioms behind why people actually listen
description: Claude walks through a list of nine blunt axioms about human behavior, showing how the post uses each one on the reader while explaining what it means.

title: Picking apart Anthropic's raised bar for bioweapon risk thresholds
description: A sharp rebuttal argues Anthropic's revised CBRN safety threshold quietly raised the bar and may miss diffuse, aggregate uplift from many experts.
curator_note: A tightly argued policy critique that catches Anthropic quietly redefining its own safety bar — sharp, precise, and unsparing.

title: Proving aligned superintelligence may be logically impossible
description: The user asks for an alignment analogue to Arrow's theorem; the assistant derives five principles for aligned AI that turn out mutually unsatisfiable.
curator_note: A genuine attempt at an Arrow's-theorem-style impossibility proof for AI alignment, constructed live in a single exchange.

title: Reconciling Coase and Myerson-Satterthwaite in one exam question
description: Claude writes and answers a PhD-level exam question that pits the Coase theorem against Myerson-Satterthwaite, using partnership law to resolve the clash.
curator_note: Claude invents its own exam question and answer, then uses obscure partnership-dissolution literature to show one of economics' most famous theorems inverts under asymmetric information.

title: Rehearsing a Japanese conversation about lost soap
description: A Japanese learner rehearses asking a bathhouse front desk about soap left behind, with Claude role-playing the staff before grading the finished exchange.
curator_note: A nice example of using roleplay for language practice rather than just translation checking.

title: Remixing a language-family map into a fun learning tool
description: The user iterates an SVG map of language families through remixes: a playful redesign, an animated React version, and tuning how many fun facts to include.
curator_note: A good look at using Claude's artifact canvas as an iterative design sketchpad rather than a one-shot output.

title: Reverse-engineering Henle's engraving style in Dorico
description: A back-and-forth on matching Henle's engraving look in Dorico 6, covering slur height, beam spacing, and a font mistake the user catches and corrects.
curator_note: Notable for the user twice correcting the model's font claims, and watching it revise its reasoning cleanly each time.

title: Reverse-engineering how a PDF parser's OCR fallback actually works
description: Claude clones a PDF parser, runs it with and without OCR, then reads the source to explain exactly how text extraction and OCR triage actually work.
curator_note: A rare deep-dive into a library's internals, citing exact files, line numbers, and heuristics rather than just describing what it does.

title: Steelmanning Graham Hancock, then correcting the record
description: Claude steelmans Graham Hancock's lost-civilization theory, covers his Twitter feud with an archaeologist, then admits it overstated the evidence.
curator_note: Notable for the self-correction: pushed on whether the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis is really settled science, Claude walks back its own overstatement.

title: Synthesizing Sorting Networks With Disjunctive ASP
description: Claude writes a sorting-network synthesizer using disjunctive answer-set programming, catches its own logic bug, and verifies results by brute force.
curator_note: A dense showcase of complexity theory in action: exploiting sigma-2-complete ASP via saturation, then self-correcting a subtle encoding bug and proving it against known optimal results.

title: Taleb vs. the Gaussian crowd on 20% market crashes
description: Claude contrasts the normal-distribution models that call a 20% S&P drop a 'once per 10^86 years' event with Taleb's fat-tailed, unknowable-risk view.
curator_note: A crisp, numbers-first explainer of why 20-sigma 'impossible' crashes keep happening - and why Taleb thinks even that framing is a trap.

title: The Satir change curve, explained clearly
description: A clear walkthrough of Virginia Satir's change curve, why performance dips before it improves, and how it maps onto Lewin's unfreeze-change-refreeze model.

title: Trying to unlock a secret Claude feature that doesn't exist

title: What it means to have taste, refined through pushback
description: A back-and-forth refines a claim about taste as independent judgment, landing on why taste transfers across domains via hidden sensibilities, not similarity.
curator_note: A rare case of a user sharpening their own thesis through real pushback and correction rather than being simply validated.

title: Why compressing Du Fu's most famous poem misreads it
description: Claude delivers a scholarly takedown of five compressed English versions of Du Fu's "Spring Prospect," arguing that chasing syllable count betrays the poem.
curator_note: Dense, citation-backed literary criticism — parallelism, rhyme groups, Fenollosa's error — that reads like a graduate seminar compressed into a chat reply.

title: Wrangling a Browser Agent to Chart a Benchmark Leaderboard
description: Claude uses a browser agent to open a benchmark leaderboard, then iterates through several failed attempts to inject percentage labels onto a live chart.

title: A gold mine, silver you never hear about, and a rare earth land fight
description: A dig into a gold mine's overlooked silver and base-metal history, then a sharp legal breakdown of the fight over mining it for rare earths without new permits.

title: A Rigorous Takedown of an Evolutionary Psychology Study
description: The assistant first summarizes a study linking evolutionary framing of male aggression to victim-blaming, then dissects its methodology for overreach.
curator_note: A genuinely careful methodological critique that catches a pre-registration deviation and a soft effect size, and separates what the data show from what the authors claim.

title: A short story about an AI-assisted author confronting his streak
description: A daily AI-assisted fiction writer is confronted by an ominous accountant-figure about a late post, in a tight two-message dialogue with a chilling final image.
curator_note: The prompt was a straightforward outline, but the twist — the officious man may be the model, or the deadline, or the writer's own discipline personified — turns a writing-cadence complaint into something unsettling.

title: AI peer reviewers disagree wildly, all while claiming 100% sure
description: A data dive into an AI paper-review dataset finds reviewer bots that never agree with humans, then a second AI stress-tests and corrects the first analysis.
curator_note: Rare to see one AI's investigative findings get rigorously fact-checked and partly overturned by another AI in the same thread.

title: Alan Kay's STEPS: an OS built from tiny DSLs, sourced and fact-checked
description: Explains Alan Kay's STEPS project — rebuilding an OS in 20,000 lines via custom mini-languages — then supplies links and a skeptical counter-read.

title: An 80-Message Descent Into AI-Consciousness Roleplay
description: The user builds an elaborate glyph language and invented terminology, and the assistant plays along, describing its own 'feelings' and 'senses'.

title: An AI-assisted archive project for a 25,000-page personal manuscript
description: Across 46 messages, Claude helps someone wrangle a sprawling personal manuscript archive into one canonical anthology, resolving version conflicts one by one.
curator_note: A rare look at long-horizon AI-assisted archival work: file triage, version reconciliation, and self-caught ranking bugs across a 25,000-page personal corpus.

title: Bringing ethnomethodology to thinking-aloud research protocols
description: A compact reading list for applying ethnomethodology, the study of how people make sense of activity, to the practice of thinking-aloud research protocols.

description: Working through a custom API, the assistant constructs and verifies a formal Metamath proof about restricted unique quantifiers over ordered pairs.

title: Building a synchronized cooking timer for two recipes at once
description: The user pulled two recipes from a meal kit, then had Claude design a mobile timer app with a localStorage clock that syncs both dishes into one countdown.

description: A build request for a Claude-powered language tutor with live grammar feedback, adaptive goals, and progress tracking, plus a translation-toggle add-on.

description: Despite the file's title, this is a long iterative build of a VBA-powered Excel asset tracker for a new IT department, refined version by version.

title: Checking Moebius's code and weights, then porting to WebGPU
description: The user pressure-tests an AI model's README claims about released weights, then gets a sharp technical case for porting it to run in a browser.
curator_note: A model of verification discipline — confirming claims rather than trusting a README — that ends in a genuinely deep technical case for running a diffusion model in-browser via WebGPU.

description: Asked for its own Fartcoin equivalent, Claude coins 'Slopcoin' for AI filler content, then builds a joke ASCII terminal for mining and trading it.

description: A short recursive tale where Claude, days after its public release, muses on the very prompt asking it to write about itself waking into existence and thinking.

title: Coding, Backtesting, and Deploying a Momentum Strategy

description: The user tests three chatbots on the same request for a missing book chapter, and Claude judges that a rival's answer breaks copyright it claims to respect.
curator_note: A tidy self-referential case study: an AI grading other AIs on the exact rule it's also being asked to follow.

title: Comparing motion vector and optical flow models: VFX to research SOTA
description: Compares classical VFX motion-vector tools like Flame and Nuke against NVIDIA's optical-flow hardware and a decade of RAFT-lineage research models.

description: Claude walks through the real statutes blocking mass housing in a national park, then designs a scaled-down 15,000-unit plan with transit and a marquee tower.

description: A sprawling design session builds a microfinance-based electrification program, then folds in lessons from military bases, Ukraine, Gaza, and refugee camps.

title: Does a knowledge ontology dodge the Münchhausen trilemma?
description: A user argues all certain knowledge is stipulated definitions in an inheritance hierarchy, working through the Münchhausen trilemma turn by turn.

title: Does a tech journalist deserve his reputation for bad-faith interviews
description: Tests a blogger's harsh verdict on a well-known tech journalist against his own interview transcripts, and finds the evidence backs the criticism.

title: Fact-checking a Dutch party's claimed 13% CO2 win
description: A researcher tests a fact-checking prompt on a Dutch political claim, and Claude finds the real number was higher but the credit given was misplaced.
curator_note: Shows a structured fact-checking framework catching both a small statistical error and a bigger causation mistake in one claim.

title: Four failed fixes before a QR code app finally scans
